source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
DartPoints Columbus in Columbus, Indiana, publishes 2.5 MW of IT capacity, operated by DartPoints.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 250 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 62 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

No compliance certifications are published for DartPoints Columbus. That does not mean none exist, only that this site's dataset, built from the operator's own facility page, does not list any, which limits what regulated workloads a reader could confirm the facility is qualified to host.

Indiana has 1 facility mapped in this site's dataset, of which 1 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 2.5 MW. DartPoints Columbus contributes 2.5 MW of that total. At that published size it is a small facility relative to what frontier AI training infrastructure requires, which now runs into the tens or hundreds of megawatts, though it may still support inference workloads or smaller-scale AI applications.
